title: Level A - Cleanest (Gold Standard)
whatItMeans: - You use only officially released APIs and tools.\n- No direct access to SAP database tables.\n- No modifications to SAP standard code.
beginnerAnalogy: - You build a Windows app using Microsoft-approved tools like .NET or PowerShell cmdlets.\n- You never touch system files or registry directly.\n- Your app is safe, clean, and works even after Windows updates.
toolsUsed: CDS Views from SAP API Hub (e.g., I_SalesOrderItem), OData Services, SAP BTP apps (CAP/RAP), SAP Build dashboards, SAP Analytics Cloud
exampleReport: 1. You build a Fiori app that shows sales orders using the released CDS view I_SalesOrderItem.\n2. You use SAP Analytics Cloud to visualize data from a public OData API exposed by S/4HANA.
whyReasoning:
- Fully upgrade-safe
- No risk of breaking SAP during upgrades
- SAP supports it officially
- Clean Core compliant and future-proof
description: Released APIs, CDS views, In-App Extension for enhancement
technology: Released CDS and Odata, RAP BTP, RAP S4HANA Using released CDS views

title: Level B - Classic but Acceptable
whatItMeans: - You use classic APIs like BAPIs or RFCs.\n- These are stable but not officially released in API Hub.\n- No modifications to SAP standard code.
beginnerAnalogy: - You use older Windows DLLs or COM objects that Microsoft still supports but doesn’t recommend for new apps.\n- Your app works, but future updates might require changes.
toolsUsed: BAPIs (e.g., BAPI_PO_GETDETAIL), RFCs, ALV Reports, Web Dynpro
exampleReport: 1. You create an ALV report that calls BAPI_PO_GETDETAIL to fetch purchase order details.\n2. You build a Fiori app that uses a custom RFC to get data from S/4HANA.
whyReasoning: - Still supported by SAP\n- Easier for brownfield systems\n- Upgrade risk is moderate
description: Developing Reports using Classical API and legacy technology without changing or accessing SAP Tables directly
technology: ABAP Reports Using Released FM, CDS views etc.

title: Level C - Risky Legacy
whatItMeans: - You access internal SAP tables or undocumented function modules directly.\n- These are not exposed via released APIs.\n- No modifications to SAP standard code, but uses hidden internals.
beginnerAnalogy: - You open Windows system folders and read files directly instead of using official APIs.\n- Works now, but breaks easily after updates.
toolsUsed: Direct SELECT on tables like `EKPO`, `MARA`, Undocumented function modules, Custom Z-reports
exampleReport: 1. You write a Z-report that does `SELECT * FROM EKPO` to get PO items.\n2. You use a function module like `ME_READ_PO_FOR_REPORTING` that’s not in API Hub.
whyReasoning: - Not upgrade-safe\n- SAP may change these tables or functions anytime\n- Should only be temporary
description: Creating report by accessing the SAP Tables directly or Using internal function modules (Starts with SD_, MM_ etc and not mentioned in API HUB)
technology: Classical ABAP with direct DB reads, Using FM with release attribute unchecked in SE37

title: Level D - Do Not Do This
whatItMeans: - You modify SAP standard code or tables.\n- You use implicit enhancements or direct updates to SAP tables.
beginnerAnalogy: - You edit Windows system files or registry keys to change OS behavior.\n- Works now, but future updates will break everything.
toolsUsed: Modifying standard SAP reports, Enhancement spots altering standard logic, Direct UPDATE/DELETE on SAP tables
exampleReport: 1. You change the standard PO report to add a new field.\n2. You write a Z-program that updates `EKPO` directly.
whyReasoning: - Breaks upgrade compatibility\n- High technical debt\n- SAP will not support it

exampleReport: Supplier onboarding app on BTP calls public S/4HANA OData API for Business Partner, changes publish events to Event Mesh, downstream systems subscribe\nOrder status interface: a BTP iFlow reads released CDS view I_SalesOrder and exposes it as a REST API to non-SAP consumers

title: Level A - Cleanest
whatItMeans: - Design workflows using released/public APIs, ABAP Cloud services, SAP Build Process Automation (SBPA) on BTP, or Flexible Workflow (standard, configuration-driven)\n- Do not modify SAP standard workflow code or directly manipulate business tables
beginnerAnalogy: - Automate tasks with Power Automate using official connectors, you don’t edit Windows system files, your flows keep working after updates
toolsUsed: Flexible Workflow (S/4HANA standard, configuration via Fiori), SAP Build Process Automation (low-code workflows, bots, forms), ABAP Cloud/RAP with released events and actions, SAP Event Mesh (publish/subscribe events), Public OData/REST APIs and released CDS views
exampleReport: Purchase Order Approval: Flexible Workflow with rule-based approvals (amount, company code), notifications via Fiori Inbox, escalations handled by SBPA using released events (e.g., “PO submitted”)\nSupplier Onboarding: SBPA orchestrates steps (data entry, compliance check) calling public BP API, emits events for downstream systems
whyReasoning: - Upgrade-safe, configurable, and SAP-supported\n- Decoupled from core code, Clean Core compliant\n- Scales with BTP, easy to monitor and change

title: Level B - Classic but Acceptable
whatItMeans: - Use classic SAP Business Workflow (WS-templates, BOR objects), workflow exits and BAdIs that are stable but not part of released ABAP Cloud\n- Avoid direct DB writes, do not modify standard workflow engines
beginnerAnalogy: - Use older, supported Windows Task Scheduler scripts. They work, but aren’t the most modern or recommended for new builds
toolsUsed: SAP Business Workflow (SWDD, BOR/CL-based), Workflow BAdIs and user exits, PI/PO or BTP iFlows to trigger/receive workflow steps via classic APIs
exampleReport: Invoice Approval: Classic SAP Workflow template (WS*) using BAPI/RFC to fetch GL data and route approvals, user decisions in SAP Inbox\nMaterial Master Change: Workflow triggered via IDoc/BAPI, approvals and notifications handled by classic inbox
whyReasoning: - Mature and widely used in brownfield\n- Lower change effort where Flexible Workflow isn’t available\n- Moderate upgrade risk, plan evolution to Level A

title: Level C - Risky Legacy
whatItMeans: - Workflow steps call internal tables directly or rely on undocumented function modules, custom includes, or hard-coded logic in standard objects\n- Orchestrate flows via custom Z-programs that read/write business tables
beginnerAnalogy: - Automation reads/writes raw registry/system files instead of using approved APIs. It Works until updates change internals
toolsUsed: Z-workflows calling SELECT/UPDATE on tables like EKKO, EKPO, Undocumented FMs to change statuses, Custom batch jobs controlling approvals via table flags
exampleReport: PO Release: Z-program checks amounts in EKKO and sets custom status fields, sends emails via direct table updates and internal FMs (no standard events)\nCredit Memo Workflow: Internal FM updates document status then triggers mail, no published events
whyReasoning: - Not upgrade-safe, table or FM changes break flows\n- Bypasses business validation, hard to audit\n- Use only temporary, refactor to Flexible Workflow/SBPA
description: Direct DB access and undocumented FMs

title: Level D - Do Not Do This
whatItMeans: - Modify standard workflow engine code, change standard WS templates, or patch standard classes that control approvals/events\n- Insert implicit enhancements into core workflow runtime or standard applications to force behavior
beginnerAnalogy: - Patch the Windows service manager to change how scheduled tasks run, unsupported and fragile
toolsUsed: Changes to standard workflow classes/templates, Implicit enhancements in standard application methods for approvals, Direct updates to standard tables in workflow engine
exampleReport: Alter SAP-delivered PO Flexible Workflow logic directly instead of configuring rules\nModify standard inbox processing to skip approvals under certain conditions
whyReasoning: - Blocks upgrades, breaks support contracts\n- Creates severe technical debt and audit issues\n- Violates Clean Core principles
description: Direct modifications to SAP standard workflow
